title: The completion of an affine scheme along a closed subset is a McQuillan affine formal algebraic space
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: For an affine scheme X over a scheme and a closed subset T, the lemma asserts that the functor of morphisms into X whose image lies in T is a McQuillan affine formal algebraic space (statement lines 3148-3157). The proof translates the condition on the image into algebra: a morphism from the spectrum of a ring corresponds to a ring map such that every prime of the target contains the extension of the radical ideal cutting out T, which means that every element of that extension is nilpotent, so the kernel of the map gives a quotient in which T is cut out by a locally nilpotent ideal (proof lines 3159-3168). Equivalently the vanishing locus of the kernel is T, and therefore the functor is the filtered colimit of the spectra of the rings by the ideals with that vanishing locus; that colimit is an affine formal algebraic space by definition (proof lines 3168-3173). It is McQuillan because the maps to the quotients are surjective and hence so are the maps from the completion, which is the defining condition for that type (proof lines 3173-3176). The claim is H2: the translation from a condition on primes into nilpotence, the identification of the functor with an explicit filtered colimit, and the verification of the McQuillan condition are each carried out.
